Spec-Driven Development with AI Agents

01 · SDD

The Problem SDD Solves

In 2024, the best AI agents solved ~20% of real GitHub issues. By mid-2025, mini-swe-agent — a 100-line Python script — solved 74% on the same benchmark. The difference was not a smarter model. It was a better contract between human and machine.

02 · SDD

Core Principles

The Spec is the Truth. Instead of code being the ultimate source of truth, the specification becomes an executable contract. If code and spec disagree, the spec wins.

Human Role: What and Why. The developer dictates intent through explicit business rules, invariants, and acceptance criteria.

03 · SDD

Why SDD Now

The tools exist today. OpenCode, Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex CLI are reasoning engines that can read specs, plan architectures, and execute tasks. The missing piece was the process. SDD provides the process. The human stays in control; the AI handles implementation.

04 · Agent Stack

The Host — The Reasoning Engine

The host is the core reasoning engine — the LLM running inside a CLI or IDE: OpenCode, Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Codex CLI. The host orchestrates everything: reads your spec, loads skills, calls MCP tools, spawns subagents, and executes commands.

05 · Agent Stack

Skills — SKILL.md

A version-controlled Markdown file that teaches the agent conventions, workflows, and domain knowledge. Skills are loaded on demand, not into every conversation — keeping context lean. A skill registry indexes them by trigger phrase so the agent knows which to load.

06 · Agent Stack

MCP — Model Context Protocol

An open standard (like USB-C for AI). MCP servers provide agents with a standardized way to connect to external systems — databases, APIs, file systems, and issue trackers. The agent discovers available tools and calls them.

07 · Agent Stack

Subagents — Context Isolation

The single most important pattern. Every file read, every command output, every conversation turn lives in one context window. As it fills, quality degrades. A subagent is a fresh, isolated session that receives a specific task, does the work, and returns a summary. The heavy reading happens in its context, not yours.

08 · Context Management

The Fundamental Constraint

The context window is everything the model sees: system prompt, history, files read, your instruction. Typically ~200K tokens. As it fills, the agent forgets earlier instructions, makes more mistakes, and loses track of the spec. This is not a bug — it is a physical limit.

09 · Context Management

Strategies

/clear: Reset context between unrelated tasks.
Subagents: Delegate heavy reading to isolated sessions.
Compaction: Agent summarizes old messages, keeps key decisions.
Plan mode: Read and plan without editing.
Session naming: Name sessions like git branches.

10 · Context Management

The Rule of Two Corrections

If you have corrected the agent more than twice on the same issue in one session: (1) the context is polluted with failed approaches, (2) /clear and start fresh with a better prompt, (3) a clean session with a precise prompt beats a long session with accumulated corrections — every time.

11 · Verification

Tests Are Not Optional

The single biggest predictor of SDD success: does the repo already have tests? Without tests, the agent has no feedback loop. It produces code, says "looks done," and waits for you to find the bugs. You become the verification loop — defeating the purpose.

12 · Verification

Verification Tiers

From weakest to strongest:
1. Prompt-level: "Run the tests and fix any failures" — works once, does not persist.
2. Goal conditions: Agent re-checks after every turn.
3. Hooks: Script runs on every file save — deterministic.
4. Adversarial review: A separate subagent reviews the diff — catches what the writer cannot see.

13 · Verification

Evidence > Claims

When the agent says "tests pass," demand to see the output:

$ pytest tests/test_fir_filter.py -v
tests/test_fir_filter.py::test_lowpass  PASSED
tests/test_fir_filter.py::test_phase     PASSED
tests/test_fir_filter.py::test_symmetry  PASSED
================== 3 passed in 0.42s ==================

Evidence is faster to review than re-running the tests yourself, and it works for sessions you were not actively watching.

14 · Memory

Engram — Persistent Cross-Session Memory

A memory system that survives across sessions. The agent saves decisions, bugs, conventions, and discoveries — and recalls them automatically in future sessions. When you return days later, Engram provides the "why we do things this way" context without you re-explaining anything.

15 · Memory

OpenSpec — Project-Folder Context

A folder convention (openspec/ or sdd/) inside each project that stores the spec, plan, and tasks for the current change. This is the project-scoped complement to Engram's cross-session memory. OpenSpec stores WHAT we are building; Engram stores WHY we made certain decisions.

16 · Memory

The Memory Cycle

Engram provides the "why we do things this way" context → OpenSpec provides the "what we're building right now" → Agent executes against spec, validates with tests → Discoveries flow back to Engram. This cycle eliminates the "re-explain everything" problem across sessions, compactions, and model changes.

17 · Spec-Writing

Anatomy of a Good spec.md

A good spec has: Intent (what problem it solves), Acceptance Criteria (testable, binary), Scope Boundaries (explicitly in/out of scope), Edge Cases (what happens at boundaries?), and Verification (exact test commands and golden file paths).

18 · Spec-Writing

Given-When-Then Pattern

Scenario: Low-pass filter with Hamming window
Given a sample rate of 8000 Hz
And a cutoff frequency of 1000 Hz
When the FIR designer generates coefficients
Then the coefficient array must be symmetric
And the passband ripple must be < 0.1 dB
And the stopband attenuation must be > 50 dB

19 · Security

Supply-Chain Reality

Every MCP server, every skill, every plugin is code that runs on your machine. An agent with file-write and command-execute permissions has the power to modify your system. The question is not "should we trust it?" but "how do we constrain the blast radius?"

20 · Security

Enterprise Context

MCP servers and skills are supply-chain dependencies — they should be versioned, scanned, signed, and audited just like npm packages or pip dependencies. A skill that teaches your agent database migration conventions is as critical as the migration framework itself.

21 · FAQ

Common Questions

When is SDD overkill? If the diff fits in one sentence (fix typo, rename variable, add log), skip SDD. SDD pays off when the change touches 3+ files, you are unsure about the approach, or there are unmapped edge cases.

What if my repo has no tests? Add tests first as a separate SDD change. Without tests, you are doing fast vibe coding, not SDD.

22 · FAQ

DSP & Hardware Projects

Can SDD work for hardware and embedded projects? Yes. Golden-file tests (known input → known output), fixed-point arithmetic conventions, and hardware constraints (memory limits, sample rates) are all spec-able. The agent does not need to know your specific microcontroller — the spec encodes the constraints.
